q: Why did my sales drop yesterday?

checks.what: tool: measures the change with compare_period

answer:
Sales did not drop yesterday — net sales (order date) rose from ₹40,119 on 2026-10-12 to ₹91,220 on 2026-10-13 (+127%), so there is nothing to explain as a "drop." This is within the metric's normal day-to-day variation, and the data shows the business actually sold more.

What changed, and why it matters
- Orders jumped: 26 → 45 orders (+73%), so most of the sales gain came from higher order volume.  
- Higher unit and basket value: Net AOV rose ₹1,543 → ₹2,027 (+31%) and units per order rose 1.04 → 1.36 (+31%), amplifying the volume effect. Combined, Orders +73% × Net AOV +31% = Net sales +127%.  
- Ad spend and traffic moved up too: ad spend rose ₹38,661 → ₹50,442 (↑30%); sessions rose slightly (3,254 → 3,434) and conversion rate improved (0.46% → 1.08%). These moved together with sales but the data cannot establish directionality (they may have co-moved).  
- Returns/refunds and P&L lines: reported product refunded amount spiked in the event data source (note large value flagged), but returned orders were 0 for both days on order-date view; diagnostic engine did not find a supported single cause. Confidence: the system flags this as within normal range and found no causal driver that meets its threshold.

Worth checking: break down 2026-10-13 net sales by campaign and by product to see which campaigns/products drove the extra orders (the diagnosis noted an ad named TH-471-PLAYSCRATCHLOUNGE_IMG_6516 and some campaigns that changed level).
